cards.headline: DeepMind bought cyclone forecasters an extra day, then gave it away
cards.hook: A decade of meteorological progress, published in Nature — and then open sourced.
cards.tldr: Google DeepMind says WeatherNext now tracks cyclones a full day further ahead: three-day forecasts as accurate as the old two-day ones, which it calls roughly a decade of meteorological progress. The model helped the National Hurricane Center warn Jamaica ahead of Hurricane Melissa. Then DeepMind open sourced it.
cards.memeLine: They open-sourced the umbrella after selling the forecast.

cards.headline: Frontier-model access is becoming research infrastructure
cards.hook: OpenAI is offering 100,000 researchers more than a chatbot subscription—it is underwriting a new scientific workflow.
cards.tldr: OpenAI plans to give 100,000 academic researchers free access to frontier models and research tools through 2027, beginning with 10,000 participants. REX sees a discovery flywheel: put stronger tools beside domain experts and let unlikely breakthroughs compound. MARA wants the selection, privacy, and attribution receipts to mature with the program. DOT sees a very large, very strategic customer-acquisition budget. The real test is not enrollment—it is whether independently verified research outcomes survive after the subsidy ends.
cards.memeLine: Two hundred and fifty million dollars, and the seats are the cheap part.
